name: UniSQL
tagline: Won Kim's early-1990s object-relational DBMS (UniSQL/X) and multidatabase server (UniSQL/M).
description: UniSQL was an Austin, Texas company founded in 1990 by Won Kim, previously chief architect of MCC's ORION object-oriented database. Its UniSQL/X server, shipped in March 1992, unified SQL with an object model (classes, inheritance, methods, collection-valued attributes), making it one of the first commercial object-relational databases, ahead of Illustra. UniSQL/M (1993) added a multidatabase layer over relational and legacy sources, which Versant licensed; Cincom also resold the server. The independent company did not last; dbdb.io records it as acquired by Korea Computer Communications in 1997, and the products have not been sold for many years.
statusNote: Late-1990s products no longer sold; dbdb.io records UniSQL as acquired by Korea Computer Communications in 1997. Object-relational ideas live on in PostgreSQL.
strengths: One of the first commercial object-relational servers, combining SQL with classes and inheritance
UniSQL/M federated queries across relational and pre-relational sources
weaknesses: Small vendor that could not compete with Oracle, Informix and IBM
useCases: Reading the UniSQL/X papers on unifying SQL and objects
